audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer phases[N].side read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Katarina/Skill/Skill while content win[0..6] and the packet levelChart both read LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, LeBlanc, Katarina, Katarina, Katarina. The full-layer whys on rows 0-3 also described Katarina winning those stages.
audit.why: Sigil of Malice is 700 range on a flat 6s cooldown against a 625-range melee, and Distortion's return blink means her level 2-5 trades cannot be answered. The lane flips at 6 because Mimic is front-loaded and leaves her on cooldowns while Death Lotus is still loaded.
audit.corrected: All disagreeing sides aligned to the content layer and packet; phases[0..3].why rewritten in the same proposal so each row's sentence argues the LeBlanc verdict.

audit.why: Level 6 is the flip, first item is the burst race inversion, late game favours resets over single picks. Her ultimate clock is Mimic at 45/35/25s.

audit.whatIsWrong: Both of the brief's missing interactions were absent from the page: Bouncing Blade's grounding shutting off Distortion, and Ethereal Chains (with Mimic repeating it) cancelling Death Lotus. breakdown.cooldowns also had no digit in it, and two bullet bodies were the tradeGood/tradeBad strings pasted under unrelated titles.
audit.why: Katarina's Q carries the grounding flag ('shuts off enemy dashes') and LeBlanc's W is a dash; Katarina's R is an interruptible channel and Ethereal Chains is hardCC that roots after 1.5 seconds shackled. These are the two decisive interactions of the matchup.
audit.corrected: Grounding stated in tradeGood and breakdown.early; the Lotus cancel stated in tradeBad, breakdown.cooldowns and breakdown.trading. Cooldowns field now carries Distortion 15s to 10s with its 4-second return window, Ethereal Chains 14s with the 1.5s root, and Sigil of Malice at a flat 6s.

audit.whatIsWrong: content.early stated her W cooldown as 'about 10 seconds early'. Distortion is 15s at rank 1 and only reaches 10s at rank 5.
audit.why: A player tracking a 10s W in the early game will step up five seconds too soon.

edits.before: LeBlanc wins by landing Distortion, denying your pattern, and cashing the all-in before your pattern matures.
edits.after: LeBlanc wins by shackling you at 925 range, rooting you out of Death Lotus, and blinking home before you answer.

edits.before: Levels 1-5 are LeBlanc's lane and pretending otherwise is how you go 0/3. Her level 2 W Distortion trade hits before your Q-E can respond and she blinks back out of your return-damage range. Play the edge of the wave, farm with Bouncing Blade, and keep a minion between you and the Q Sigil poke line. Your one job is Shunpo-dodging the E Ethereal Chains — an unbound chain means her follow-up burst fizzles and the trade is nearly free. Track her W cooldown (about 10 seconds early): the 4-second window after she uses it on the wave is your only safe trade slot.
